items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: So eventually I went from there to recording a big band, Lavier Johnson, he called himself Charles Lavier afterwards, pianist. And we did a big band.

ctx.x: The train. They had a terrible run, it was bad on the thing, but they were good records they’re still here. Boyce Brown was the one — I want to tell you something about Boyce afterwards. He was an alto player, you probably never heard of him. But he was the first. He was a white boy and he was blind, and very soulful, and he played wonderful alto, long before you heard about Benny Carter. If you hear those records you will see that he had a natural gift and it was wonderful. He joined a monastery in the end and…
Let me ask you, you said you wanted to record these people. Well how do you get from wanting to do it, to actually—
